tasks.title: Kendini tanıt
tasks.prompt: Yeni bir sınıfa girdin. Kendini tanıt: adın, nereli olduğun, ne iş yaptığın ya da ne okuduğun ve bir hobin.

teach.title: Kendini tanıtmanın sırası
points: Adla başla: My name is ... / I'm ...
Nereli olduğunu söyle: I'm from ... / I live in ...
Ne yaptığını ekle: I work as ... / I study ...
Bir kişisel ayrıntıyla bitir: In my free time, I ...

tasks.model: Hello, everyone. My name is Deniz and I'm from Izmir, Turkey. I live in Istanbul now. I work as a software developer at a small company. In my free time, I like running and cooking. I also read a lot of books about history. Nice to meet you all.

tasks.title: Bir günün nasıl geçiyor
tasks.prompt: Sıradan bir gününü anlat. Sabahtan akşama sırayla yaz.

teach.title: Sıra bildiren kelimeler
points: Sırayı göstermek metni okunur yapar: first, then, after that, finally
Rutin için geniş zaman kullan: I get up, I have breakfast
Saat için 'at': at seven o'clock, at 7:30
Aynı bağlacı tekrarlama; 'and' ile bağlanan uzun zincirler yorucu

phrases.en: I usually get up at seven.
After that, I go to work.

tasks.model: I usually get up at seven o'clock. First, I drink a glass of water and take a shower. Then I have breakfast with my family. After that, I go to work by bus. I work until six in the evening. When I get home, I cook dinner and watch a series. Finally, I read for half an hour and go to bed at eleven.

tasks.title: Tatilden kartpostal
tasks.prompt: Bir tatildesin. Arkadaşına kartpostal yaz: neredesin, hava nasıl, ne yaptın, ne hissediyorsun.

teach.title: Kartpostal kısa ama tam olur
points: Selamla ve nerede olduğunu söyle: Hi Ali! I'm in Rome.
Yaptıklarını geçmiş zamanla anlat: Yesterday we visited ...
Bir duygu cümlesi ekle: It was amazing.
Kapanış at: See you soon! / Love, Deniz

tasks.model:
Hi Elif! I'm writing to you from Barcelona. The weather is lovely here, about 25 degrees every day. Yesterday we visited the old town and walked along the beach in the evening. The food was amazing, especially the seafood. Today we are going to a museum. I miss you a lot. See you soon!

Love,
Deniz

tasks.title: Şehir mi kasaba mı
tasks.prompt: Şehirde mi yoksa küçük bir kasabada mı yaşamak daha iyi? Görüşünü yaz ve en az iki gerekçe ver.

teach.title: Görüş paragrafının iskeleti
points: Görüşünü ilk cümlede söyle; sonuna saklama
Her gerekçeyi ayrı cümlede ver ve bir örnekle destekle
Karşı görüşe bir cümle ayır: Some people say ..., but ...
Kapanışta görüşünü tekrarla, yeni bir fikir açma

tasks.model: In my opinion, living in a small town is better than living in a big city. The main reason is the cost. For example, rent in a city like Istanbul takes almost half of an average salary, while in a small town the same money is enough for a whole family. The second reason is time. People in cities spend two hours a day in traffic, and that time is simply lost. Some people say cities offer better jobs and culture, and that is true. On the other hand, remote work has made this argument weaker every year. For these reasons, I believe a small town gives a better daily life.

tasks.title: Ters giden bir gün
tasks.prompt: Her şeyin ters gittiği bir günü anlat. Ne oldu, neden oldu, sonunda ne yaptın?

teach.title: Anlatıyı okunur yapan şey
points: Sahneyi kur: Last Monday I had an important meeting.
Olayları sırayla ver ve zaman bağlacı kullan: while, as soon as, by the time
Sürerken kesilen bir eylem için past continuous: I was walking when ...
Bir sonuç cümlesiyle bitir: In the end, ...

phrases.en: As soon as I woke up, ...

tasks.model: Last Monday everything went wrong. As soon as I woke up, I saw that my phone had not charged, so my alarm never rang. I was already an hour late. While I was running to the bus stop, it started to rain and I had no umbrella. By the time I arrived at the office, my clothes were completely wet and the meeting had started. My manager was not happy. In the end, I apologised, presented my part of the project, and stayed an extra hour to finish the report. It was a bad day, but nothing was broken that could not be fixed.

tasks.title: Bir yer hakkında yorum
tasks.prompt: Gittiğin bir restoran, otel ya da kafe hakkında yorum yaz. Beğendiğin ve beğenmediğin yanları söyle, sonunda tavsiye edip etmediğini belirt.

teach.title: İnandırıcı yorum nasıl yazılır
points: Genel izlenimle başla, sonra ayrıntıya in
Somut ol: 'the food was good' değil, 'the lamb was tender and well seasoned'
Olumsuzu da yaz; yalnızca övgü içeren yorum güvenilir görünmez
Nitelenmiş dil kullan: slightly, rather, a little, fairly
Net bir tavsiyeyle bitir

phrases.en: It was rather expensive for what it offers.

tasks.model: Overall, Kasap Deniz is a solid neighbourhood restaurant that does a few things very well. What impressed me most was the grilled sea bass: it arrived at the table still crackling, and the lemon and olive oil dressing was light rather than heavy. The bread is baked in house and the staff are genuinely friendly without hovering over you. However, the place has two clear weaknesses. The dining room is small and rather loud once it fills up, so it is not the place for a quiet conversation. The wine list is also short and slightly overpriced for what it offers. If you go early and you care more about the food than the atmosphere, I would definitely recommend it.

tasks.title: Sorun ve çözüm
tasks.summary: Sorunu tanımla, çözüm öner, itirazı karşıla
tasks.prompt: Yaşadığın şehirde seni rahatsız eden bir sorun seç. Sorunu tanımla, iki çözüm öner ve önerilerinin zayıf yanını da söyle.

teach.title: Sorun-çözüm metninin yapısı
points: Sorunu ölçülebilir biçimde tanımla: kim, ne kadar, ne sıklıkta
Her çözümü ayrı paragrafta ver
Çözümün maliyetini ya da zorluğunu da yaz — bunu atlayan metin naif görünür
Bağlaçlarla akış kur: firstly, moreover, admittedly, nevertheless

phrases.en: One of the most pressing problems is ...
A possible solution would be to ...

phrases.tr: Kabul etmek gerekir ki bu ... gerektirir.

phrases.en: Nevertheless, the benefits outweigh the costs.
phrases.tr: Yine de faydalar maliyetten ağır basar.

tasks.model: One of the most pressing problems in my district is parking. There are roughly four thousand flats and fewer than nine hundred legal parking spaces, so cars end up on pavements every evening and pedestrians walk in the road. A possible solution would be to build a multi storey car park on the empty municipal plot near the market. Admittedly, this would require significant investment and at least two years of construction, during which the situation would get worse rather than better. A cheaper measure would be resident permits combined with real enforcement. This costs almost nothing and could start next month, although it does not create a single new space and would simply push the problem into neighbouring streets. Nevertheless, taken together the two measures would make the area walkable again.

tasks.title: Tartışmalı bir konuda deneme
tasks.summary: Tez, karşı tez ve nitelenmiş sonuç
tasks.prompt: Uzaktan çalışma kalıcı olmalı mı? Bir tez kur, en güçlü karşı argümanı kendin yaz ve onu yanıtla.

teach.title: C1 seviyesinde tartışma
points: En güçlü karşı argümanı sen yaz; zayıfını seçmek metni değersizleştirir
Mutlak ifade kullanma: 'always', 'never' yerine 'in most cases', 'tends to'
İddiayı kanıtla değil, mekanizmayla destekle: neden böyle oluyor?
Sonuç, giriştekinden daha nitelikli olmalı; aynı cümleyi tekrarlama

phrases.en: The strongest objection to this view is ...
This objection has real force, but ...
phrases.tr: Bu itirazın gerçek bir ağırlığı var, ama ...

phrases.en: The evidence points in a more modest direction.
phrases.tr: Kanıtlar daha ölçülü bir yöne işaret ediyor.

tasks.model: It is often argued that remote work should become the default arrangement, and I would broadly defend that position, though with narrower limits than its advocates usually accept. The case rests on a mechanism rather than a preference: concentrated work requires uninterrupted blocks of time, and open plan offices are structurally hostile to them. Where output is measurable and largely individual, distance tends to help. The strongest objection to this view is not about productivity at all but about the formation of new people. Junior staff learn by overhearing, by watching how a difficult conversation is handled, by the accidental corridor question that they would never schedule a call to ask. Remote work removes exactly this layer, and it does so invisibly: the cost appears three years later as a thin management bench. This objection has real force. It does not, however, argue for a return to five days in an office; it argues for deliberate structure. Teams that pair juniors with seniors on shared work, and that meet in person on a predictable rhythm, reproduce most of that learning. The evidence points in a more modest direction than either camp claims: remote work is right for the task and wrong for the apprenticeship, and the sensible arrangement addresses each separately.
